text: During the excavations at Kirkjuhóll a grave was uncovered that included a skull that had clearly been damaged in two places by an edged weapon. The carbon-dating shows that this skull dates from around the year 1000. The forensic archaeological research has revealed that the cut in the skull was extremely clean and caused by a sharp axe or a sword. This wound killed the man. It is sometimes said that the weapons during the Middle Ages in Iceland were of poor quality. However, we can say with certainty that at least two people had very good weapons at that time. In the grave, two stones were found that seem to have been placed on top of the body. These stones suggest the known practice of putting weights on murder victims in order to keep them in their graves and prevent them from rising from the dead to avenge their death.
